facts.text: Barstow was organized in 1892 by irrigation pioneer George E. Barstow, who helped turn the area into a thriving farming community.
That same year, Barstow was elected the first seat of Ward County, cementing its role as the region’s administrative hub.
In 1904, Barstow’s grape growers earned a Silver Medal at the World’s Fair, showcasing the town’s agricultural excellence.
The 1904 Pecos River Dam break devastated local fruit and vegetable crops, a setback that echoed through the community for years.
By 1918, successive droughts had rendered farming nearly impossible, forcing many residents to seek livelihoods elsewhere.
Barstow sits at 31°27′45″ N 103°23′44″ W, a latitude and longitude that places it deep in the Texas Panhandle’s rural heartland.
